doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Contrapuntal left hand and closing
summary: Rowe asks about the left hand on Crazy Rhythm; Hyman is working toward a contrapuntal style; thanks and goodbyes.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I have to tell you that today the solo you played on, was it “Crazy Rhythm” I’m still trying to figure out what you were doing in your left hand while you were — it almost sounded like you were thinking of J.S. Bach. Do you consciously think of —
I’ve been trying to get a contrapuntal way of playing going and it’s coming along.
It seemed to work that time. Anything that you’d like to offer yourself that we haven’t hit on today?
No, you’ve really touched all the bases as far as — I thank you. I didn’t realize that — I thank you for being so well informed.
Well it’s been a real pleasure to speak with you and Mr. Hyman has to go back to work shortly, so we’re going to end this, and thanks a lot.
